bug_semantics: Second-order Oracle SQL identifier injection in the post-CREATE/post-UPDATE row lookup. Oracle table names are read verbatim from user_tables.TABLE_NAME and carried into the external-table query metadata. When Oracle returns response.lastRowid, OracleIntegration.query constructs SELECT * FROM "<table name>" WHERE ROWID = '<driver-produced ROWID>' by direct interpolation. An embedded double quote in the table name terminates the quoted identifier and makes the remainder SQL syntax. A user able to write that external table can trigger the lookup; the injected SQL runs with the configured Oracle datasource user's privileges and can cross Budibase's table/row authorization boundary. response.lastRowid is not the attacker-controlled part.
flaw_origin: 115fc08aa4d08ca08c65c84e3805c6df0e1ea0b8 is the smallest real origin: it replaced the prior returning implementation with a post-write ROWID lookup and first wrote the raw quoted-identifier interpolation, initially using json.endpoint.entityId. At that revision ExternalRequest derives endpoint.entityId directly from tableName, while Oracle schema introspection stores row.TABLE_NAME verbatim, so the original line already has the same identifier-injection semantics. dbe9eedcbadc6d164447078039801a53a2dcfa65 later changed the expression from json.endpoint.entityId to json.table.name but preserved the unsafe double-quote interpolation; it is a source-name rewrite, not the BIC.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/security/advisories/GHSA-xj29-x47g-9w2c names packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts's post-write ROWID SELECT as the sink, explains that json.table.name comes from user_tables.TABLE_NAME, identifies the embedded-double-quote attack, declares affected <3.40.0 and patched 3.40.0, and describes quoteOracleIdentifier as remediation.

In the read-only clone, `git show 115fc08aa4d08ca08c65c84e3805c6df0e1ea0b8 -- packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts` shows that this commit adds the response.lastRowid branch and `sql: `SELECT * FROM \"${json.endpoint.entityId}\" WHERE ROWID = '${response.lastRowid}'``. `git log -S'WHERE ROWID' -- packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts` identifies 115fc08aa4d08ca08c65c84e3805c6df0e1ea0b8 as the introduction; `git log -L 430,439:packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts 115fc08aa4d08ca08c65c84e3805c6df0e1ea0b8` likewise attributes the new lookup to that commit.

At the BIC, `git grep -n 'entityId: tableName' 115fc08aa4d08ca08c65c84e3805c6df0e1ea0b8 -- packages/server/src/api/controllers/row/ExternalRequest.ts` returns lines 162 and 646. `git show 115fc08aa4d08ca08c65c84e3805c6df0e1ea0b8:packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts` lines 155-208 shows schema SQL selecting from user_tables and mapColumns assigning `const tableName = row.TABLE_NAME` and storing `{ name: tableName }`. These establish the original sink's identifier source rather than relying on the later variable name.

Direct parent check: `git grep -n -E 'lastRowid|WHERE ROWID|json\.endpoint\.entityId' 78de4719482c86e7d4178b9445eb82acd16cc5d1 -- packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts` returns no matches. The BIC commit object has exactly one parent, 78de4719482c86e7d4178b9445eb82acd16cc5d1, so this is direct parent absence rather than inference from a release diff.

Lifecycle persistence: `git show dbe9eedcbadc6d164447078039801a53a2dcfa65 -- packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts` changes only the identifier expression in this sink from `${json.endpoint.entityId}` to `${json.table.name}` and leaves it raw inside double quotes. `git log -S'SELECT * FROM "${json.table.name}" WHERE ROWID' -- packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts` then shows dbe9eedcbadc6d164447078039801a53a2dcfa65 adding that exact spelling and 36c9d61de69957243f121883aed07f44951dfcaa removing it.

Closing fix: `git show 36c9d61de69957243f121883aed07f44951dfcaa -- packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts packages/server/src/integrations/utils/sqlIdentifiers.ts` adds `quoteOracleIdentifier`, implemented as a double-quoted identifier with every embedded `"` replaced by `""`, and changes the sink to `SELECT * FROM ${quoteOracleIdentifier(json.table.name)} ...`. This one-parent, two-file commit directly closes the identifier breakout; it is not merely a release/version commit.

Introduction release edge: `git grep -n -E 'lastRowid|WHERE ROWID' v0.9.190-alpha.9 v0.9.190-alpha.10 -- packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts` has no alpha.9 match and shows the vulnerable lookup in v0.9.190-alpha.10. `git for-each-ref --contains=115fc08aa4d08ca08c65c84e3805c6df0e1ea0b8 --sort=creatordate refs/tags` shows v0.9.190-alpha.10 as the first containing tag, followed by stable v0.9.190 and v1.0.0.

Observed fix tag edge: `git tag --contains 36c9d61de69957243f121883aed07f44951dfcaa --list '3.*' --sort=version:refname` begins at 3.39.25. `git grep -n -E 'SELECT \* FROM|quoteOracleIdentifier' 3.39.24 3.39.25 -- packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts packages/server/src/integrations/utils/sqlIdentifiers.ts` shows the raw interpolation in 3.39.24 and the helper plus quoted call in 3.39.25. The corresponding release commits are 3c86b6ab5d3f36c2bb668d6b44a17cfc32082785 (3.39.24) and a5c08bf7d989e531cc54f640a504fe9306cdfe1b (3.39.25). Tag 3.40.0 resolves to 661fe55d609404d073eea86702e0bde7942c3f10 and also contains the fix. Thus the advisory's supported/public boundary is 3.40.0, while the frozen Git tags demonstrate that the code fix first shipped in 3.39.25.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file -p 115fc08aa4d08ca08c65c84e3805c6df0e1ea0b8` shows human author and committer `Rory Powell <rory.codes@gmail.com>`, one parent, subject `Improve returning logic for oracle`, and no body trailers at all. Therefore there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI marker on the BIC commit object. No later commit's metadata was used for the AI judgment.
reasoning: The vulnerability is caused by direct string construction of an Oracle quoted identifier, not by the ROWID value. History proves the unsafe lookup first appeared atomically in 115fc08aa4d08ca08c65c84e3805c6df0e1ea0b8 and that its immediate parent had no such branch or sink. The 2024 table-property rewrite did not create the flaw, and the 2026 helper commit is the direct closing fix. The BIC is an ordinary one-parent commit, so no squash decomposition is needed. Its commit object identifies only a human author/committer and contains no AI-related trailer or bot identity. Under the required BIC-only rule, the closed verdict is NOT_AI. Version evidence preserves both facts: the advisory declares <3.40.0/3.40.0, but repository tags show the direct fix already present beginning with 3.39.25 and absent in 3.39.24.
